label: PRISMA 2020
source: PRISMA 2020 statement, https://www.prisma-statement.org (pointer only; wording is our own)

items.text: Names the report as a systematic review, a meta-analysis, or both.
Gives a structured summary of the background, methods, results and conclusions.
Explains why the review is needed given what is already known.
States the question the review sets out to answer.
Lists what made a study eligible, and how the criteria were grouped.
Names each source used to find studies, such as registers and websites.
Says how studies were searched, with dates, databases and the full search strategy.
Describes how studies were screened and who did it.
Says how data were pulled from reports and who checked them.
Lists the outcomes and variables collected from each study.
Says how the quality or bias of each study was judged.
States which effect measures were used to compare results.
Describes how results were combined, including any meta-analysis model.
Says how selective or missing results across studies were assessed.
Says how confident the review is in each body of evidence.
Reports how many records were found, screened and included, ideally in a flow diagram.
Describes each included study and its key features.
Reports the bias judgements made for each included study.
Gives the results of each study, ideally with a simple summary table.
Reports the combined results and how precise they are.
Reports what the checks for missing or selective results found.
Reports the confidence rating for each main outcome.
Interprets the findings and discusses their limits and what they mean next.
Says whether a protocol was registered, and where it can be found.
Names who funded the review and what role the funder played.
Declares any interests of the authors that could bias the review.
Says where the extracted data and analysis code can be accessed.
